questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct for a homogeneous mixture of sugar in water?

options.text: Both water and sugar are solvents.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Water is the solvent.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homogeneous mixture** is a mixture in which the composition is uniform throughout, and the components cannot be easily separated.
 
• In the case of a mixture of **sugar in water**, water acts as the **solvent**, which means it is the substance that dissolves the solute (sugar).
 
• The component present in the **larger amount** in a solution is typically considered the solvent, and water is present in a larger quantity than sugar in this mixture.
 
• Sugar, being the substance that is dissolved, is the **solute**.
 
• Water is known as the **universal solvent** because it can dissolve a vast number of substances, including sugar, salt, and many other compounds.
 
• The resulting solution of sugar and water is **transparent**, and the sugar molecules are evenly distributed throughout the water.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures like this one do not separate into distinct phases upon standing.
 
• This principle is utilized in various industries, such as the food and beverage industry, where sugar solutions are commonly used.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Both water and sugar are solvents**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect because in a solution, only one component acts as a **solvent**, and the other as a solute.
 
• Water is the solvent in this case, and sugar is the solute. They cannot both be solvents simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Sugar is the solvent**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect because sugar is the **solute**, which means it is the substance being dissolved in the solvent (water).
 
• Sugar does not have the properties of a universal solvent like water.
 
 
 
• **Water is the solute**__
 
 
• This is incorrect because water is the **solvent**, not the solute, as it dissolves the sugar to form a homogeneous mixture.
 
• Solutes are present in smaller amounts, whereas solvents are present in larger amounts. In this case, water is present in a larger quantity.

questions.question: Lavanya got married 10 years ago. Now her age is 1(1)/(5) times her age at the time of marriage. Her son’s present age is one-tenth of her present age. Find her son’s present age.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Lavanya got married 10 years ago.

Present age = 11/5 × age at marriage.

Son's age = 1/10 × Lavanya's present age.

**Formula used:**

Let Lavanya's age at marriage be x.

Present age = x + 10.

Present age = (6/5) × x.

Son's present age = (1/10) × Lavanya's present age.

**Calculations:**

Let Lavanya's age at marriage be x.

Lavanya's present age = x + 10.

Lavanya's present age = (6/5) × x.

⇒ x + 10 = (6/5) × x.

⇒ 10 = (6/5) × x - x.

⇒ 10 = (6x - 5x)/5.

⇒ 10 = x/5.

⇒ x = 10 × 5 = 50.

Lavanya's age at marriage = 50 years.

Lavanya's present age = 50 + 10 = 60 years.

Son's present age = (1/10) × 60.

⇒ Son's present age = 60/10.

⇒ Son's present age = 6 years.

**∴ Her son's present age is 6 years.**

__
 
• This reaction is an example of a **double displacement reaction**, where two compounds exchange their ions to form new compounds.
 
• The reaction between **sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄)** and **barium chloride (BaCl₂)** produces two new compounds: **barium sulfate (BaSO₄)** and **sodium chloride (NaCl)**.
 
• **Barium sulfate (BaSO₄)** forms as an insoluble precipitate, which is the hallmark of a double displacement reaction.
 
• This reaction can be represented as: **AB + CD → AD + CB**, where ions are exchanged between the reactants.
 
• In this case: **AB = Na₂SO₄**, **CD = BaCl₂**, **AD = BaSO₄**, and **CB = NaCl**.
 
• The formation of a solid precipitate (BaSO₄) confirms the occurrence of a chemical reaction.
 
• **Double displacement reactions** are commonly observed in aqueous solutions and are often used for **qualitative analysis** in chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

• **Pb(s) + CuCl₂ (aq) → PbCl₂ (aq) + Cu(s)**__
 __
 
• This is also an example of a **single displacement reaction**.
 
• Here, **lead (Pb)** replaces **copper (Cu)** in copper chloride (CuCl₂) to produce lead chloride (PbCl₂) and copper metal (Cu).
 
 
 
• **Zn(s) + CuSO₄ (aq) → ZnSO₄ (aq) + Cu(s)**__
 
 
• This is yet another example of a **single displacement reaction**.
 
• In this reaction, **zinc (Zn)** replaces **copper (Cu)** in copper sulfate (CuSO₄) to form zinc sulfate (ZnSO₄) and copper metal (Cu).

questions.question: Which of the following describes dendrites?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Short and branched**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dendrites** are specialized structures of neurons that are primarily responsible for receiving **electrochemical signals** from other neurons or sensory inputs.
 
• They are typically **short** and exhibit a **branched structure**, which increases the surface area for receiving signals.
 
• The branching nature of dendrites allows them to form **connections with multiple neurons**, facilitating the integration of information in the nervous system.
 
• Dendrites contain specialized structures called **dendritic spines**, which are tiny protrusions where synapses are formed with other neurons.
 
• They play a crucial role in processes such as **learning** and **memory** by strengthening or weakening synaptic connections based on activity.
 
• In contrast to axons, which transmit signals away from the neuron, dendrites are primarily involved in **receiving and processing incoming signals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Short and unbranched**__

 __
 
• Neuronal structures like **axon terminals** may sometimes appear short and unbranched, but this description does not apply to dendrites.
 
• Unbranched structures are typically not suited for integrating multiple inputs, which is the primary function of dendrites.
 
 
 
• **Long and branched**__
 __
 
• Axons, not dendrites, are more likely to be long and may occasionally exhibit branching, especially near their terminals.
 
• Axons are involved in transmitting signals over long distances, which differs from the function of dendrites.
 
 
 
• **Long and unbranched**__
 
 
• This description is characteristic of certain **axons**, which are responsible for conducting signals away from the neuron over long distances.
 
• Dendrites, in contrast, are short and branched to facilitate the reception of multiple signals.

questions.question: Two numbers are respectively 30% and 37% less than a third number. What percentage of the first number is the second number?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First number is 30% less than the third number.

Second number is 37% less than the third number.

**Formula used:**

Percentage = (Second number / First number) × 100.

**Calculations:**

Let the third number be 100.

First number = 100 - (30% of 100) = 100 - 30 = 70.

Second number = 100 - (37% of 100) = 100 - 37 = 63.

Required percentage = (63 / 70) × 100.

⇒ Required percentage = (9 / 10) × 100.

⇒ Required percentage = 9 × 10.

⇒ Required percentage = 90.

**∴ The second number is 90% of the first number.**

• ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is synthesized through **cellular respiration**, primarily in the mitochondria, using energy derived from the breakdown of glucose or other nutrients.
 
• The process of ATP production occurs through **oxidative phosphorylation** in the inner mitochondrial membrane, where the electron transport chain is located.
 
• Mitochondria are double-membrane organelles, with the inner membrane folded into structures called **cristae**, which increase surface area for energy production.
 
• The mitochondria are responsible for driving **endothermic reactions** within the cell by providing the necessary energy through ATP hydrolysis.
 
• These organelles are found in most eukaryotic cells and play a crucial role in **energy metabolism**, as well as other functions such as regulation of the cell cycle and apoptosis.

• While chloroplasts are involved in energy production, they do not produce ATP for cellular processes but instead synthesize glucose, which can be metabolized by mitochondria to generate ATP.
 
• Chloroplasts contain the pigment **chlorophyll**, which captures sunlight, and are unique to plant and algal cells.

questions.question: If the cross-sectional area of a conductor is doubled, other factors remaining the same, the resistivity of the conductor will be:

The Correct answer is __**same**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistivity** is a material property that measures how strongly a material opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• The **resistivity** of a conductor is dependent only on the **material's nature** and is independent of its **shape and size**, such as its cross-sectional area or length.
 
• When the cross-sectional area of a conductor is doubled, the **resistance** is affected (resistance decreases), but the **resistivity remains unchanged**.
 
• This is because resistivity is defined as a constant for a specific material at a given temperature, regardless of changes in its dimensions.
 
• The formula for resistivity is **ρ = R × (A / L)**, where **ρ** represents resistivity, **R** is resistance, **A** is the cross-sectional area, and **L** is the length of the conductor.
 
• From the formula, resistivity is independent of the conductor's dimensions; it is solely determined by the intrinsic properties of the material.

questions.question: The motion of the moon around the earth is due to the:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **motion of the moon** around the Earth is governed by the **centripetal force**.
 
• **Centripetal force** is a force that acts toward the **center of a circular path**, keeping an object in circular motion.
 
• In the case of the moon, this force is provided by the **gravitational pull of the Earth**.
 
• The **gravitational force** acts as the centripetal force, pulling the moon toward the Earth and preventing it from moving off in a straight line due to its inertia.
 
• Without this force, the moon would follow a straight-line path into space, as per **Newton's first law of motion**.
 
• The balance between the moon's tangential velocity and the centripetal force keeps it in a stable **orbital motion** around the Earth.
 
• This principle applies to all celestial bodies in orbit, including **planets, satellites, and stars** in their respective systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Centrifugal force**__

 __
 
• **Centrifugal force** is a fictitious force that appears to act outward on a body in a rotating reference frame.
 
• It is not a real force but rather the result of inertia when viewed in a non-inertial, rotating frame.
 
• In contrast to the **centripetal force**, it does not play a role in the moon's motion, as the moon orbits due to the Earth's gravitational pull.
 
 
 
• **Coriolis force**__
 __
 
• The **Coriolis force** is an apparent force caused by the rotation of the Earth.
 
• It primarily affects the motion of objects over large distances, such as **air currents and ocean currents**, causing them to deflect to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• It is not responsible for the orbital motion of celestial bodies.
 
 
 
• **Coulomb force**__
 
 
• The **Coulomb force** refers to the electrostatic force between two charged particles.
 
• It has no role in the motion of the moon, as the moon and the Earth interact primarily through **gravitational force**, not electrostatic force.

__
 
• When light passes through a **glass prism**, it undergoes **refraction**, and its constituent colors bend at different angles due to their varying wavelengths.
 
• The phenomenon of different colors bending by different amounts is called **dispersion of light**.
 
• **Yellow light**, which lies in the middle of the visible spectrum, has a wavelength of approximately **570–590 nm**.
 
• Because the bending of light is inversely proportional to its wavelength, **longer wavelengths bend less** than shorter wavelengths.

• This property of light is significant in optics, including in the design of **prisms and lenses**.

• in a circuit.
 
• **Power (P)** in an electrical circuit represents the rate at which electrical energy is transferred or converted into another form of energy, such as heat or light.
 
• The formula indicates that power is the product of **voltage (V)** and **current (I)**, where:
 
 
• **Voltage (V)** is the potential difference across two points in the circuit, measured in volts.
 
• **Current (I)** is the flow of electric charge through a conductor, measured in amperes.
 
 
 
• This formula is derived from the basic definition of power: **Power = Work / Time**. In the context of electricity, work is the product of charge and potential difference, and dividing it by time leads to the formula **P = VI**.
 
• It is a widely used formula in analyzing electrical circuits, determining the efficiency of devices, and calculating energy consumption.
 
• This relationship is valid for both **direct current (DC)** and **alternating current (AC)** circuits, though in AC circuits, factors such as phase difference and power factor may need to be considered.
 
• For example, if the voltage across a circuit is 10 volts and the current is 2 amperes, the power is calculated as:
 
 
• **P = VI = 10 × 2 = 20 watts**

questions.question: Which of the following can increase the work done by a force on an object?

__
 
• The **work done** by a force on an object is calculated using the formula: **Work = Force × Displacement × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
• Increasing the **displacement** directly increases the work done if the force and displacement are in the same direction (θ = 0 degrees).
 
• The work done depends on the magnitude of the **displacement**, as a larger displacement under the same force results in higher work.
 
• If the **displacement** increases while the force remains constant, the object moves farther, contributing to more work being done.
 
• In physics, work is a measure of the energy transfer that occurs when an object is moved over a distance by an external force.
 
• Thus, increasing the **displacement** is a practical way to enhance the work done, provided the force remains constant and is applied in the same direction.
 
• This concept is widely applied in real-life scenarios, such as in machinery, where increasing the range of motion can yield higher energy output.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reducing the mass**__

 __
 
• Reducing the **mass** does not directly affect the work done, as work depends on **force** and **displacement**, not the mass of the object.
 
• However, a lighter object requires less force to move, which can indirectly influence how much work is done under varying conditions.
 
 
 
• **Reducing the displacement**__
 __
 
• Reducing the **displacement** decreases the work done, as work is proportional to the magnitude of displacement.
 
• This option is incorrect because it contradicts the principle of maximizing work by increasing displacement.
 
 
 
• **Reducing the force**__
 
 
• Reducing the **force** also decreases the work done, as work is directly proportional to the applied force.
 
• This option is incorrect because lowering the force reduces the energy transfer to the object, resulting in less work being done.

questions.question: Two pipes C and D can fill a tank in 6 hours and 9 hours, respectively. They are opened alternately for | hour each, starting with C first. In what duration, will the tank be filled?

**Given:**

Pipe C fills tank in 6 hours.

Pipe D fills tank in 9 hours.

Pipes are opened alternately for 1 hour each, starting with C.

**Formula used:**

LCM method to find total capacity.

Efficiency = Total capacity / Time.

**Calculations:**

LCM of 6 and 9 = 18 (Total capacity).

Efficiency of C = 18 / 6 = 3 units/hour.

Efficiency of D = 18 / 9 = 2 units/hour.

In 2 hours (C then D), work done = 3 + 2 = 5 units.

In 6 hours (3 cycles of 2 hours), work done = 5 × 3 = 15 units.

Remaining work = 18 - 15 = 3 units.

Next hour, C works and fills 3 units.

Total time = 6 + 1 = 7 hours.

**∴ The tank will be filled in 7 hours.**

• **Skeletal muscle fibers** are long, cylindrical, and multinucleated, with alternating light and dark bands, indicating their striated nature.
 
• **Contractile proteins**, such as **actin and myosin**, are present in all muscle tissues and are responsible for the contraction and relaxation process.
 
• Muscle tissues are integral to various bodily functions, including **movement, posture maintenance, and internal organ functioning** like the heart and digestive system.

• **Microscopes reveal alternate light and dark bands in voluntary muscles**__
 __
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are striated, meaning they have alternating light (I-bands) and dark (A-bands) bands visible under a microscope, which are due to the arrangement of **actin and myosin filaments**.
 
• This striation is a key feature distinguishing skeletal muscles from smooth muscles, which lack this pattern.
